title: P1: JSONL reader rounds high-significance decimal cells through f64
description: Read-only audit finding (2026-11-26, no source edits): production cargo tree -e features,normal resolves serde_json 1.0.154 with default + preserve_order, but without float_roundtrip, arbitrary_precision, or raw_value. cmdrvl-tabular src/jsonl_reader.rs:116-120 parses each object line into Value; :143-153 converts non-integer Numbers via as_f64()+canon_f64 into Cell bytes. This is a shared upstream data conversion: a 16-19 significant-digit JSON decimal can become the adjacent f64 value, changing downstream comparison/verdict/output values in rvl and shape. XLSX/Parquet native numeric paths are separate. No released tabular binary was present locally, so this audit is code-read only. NOT VERIFIED: no build, test, release-binary reproduction, or fix was run.

title: open and open_bytes panic on some corrupted Parquet files instead of returning a typed refusal
description:
Found by the orchestrator while verifying spine-rules bd-nh4. Three corrupted Parquet files (fixture bytes with random flips or truncation) panic in open()/open_bytes() or while reading rows, at 57c3085 (before open_bytes) and at e83afb0 alike, so it predates that change: 24 panicking file/option cases of 25402. Expected: a typed refusal, never a panic. NOT CHECKED: the panic message and location, and whether released shape or rvl binaries are affected. Smallest reproducer, 753 bytes, base64 (decode to a .parquet file, open with default options):

comments.author: zac
comments.text: Verified bd-tg9 at commit a211ce6e65c83a797a2895bc0a9e707ca588f0b6, pushed to main; no dependency, feature, gate, or version changes. The supplied 753-byte fixture first failed on the old code: the exact command lockf -k /private/tmp/spine-cargo-2.lock env CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3 cargo test --test open_bytes bd_tg9_corrupt_parquet_is_a_typed_refusal_for_path_and_bytes -- --exact panicked at parquet 60.2.0 file/metadata/mod.rs:1153, ColumnChunkMetaData::byte_range, with column start and length should not be negative. This is inside the dependency lazy row iterator; no catch_unwind or dependency change was needed. The fix validates effective dictionary/data offsets and compressed lengths before that iterator is constructed, returning the existing E_PARQUET_PARSE refusal. The new test proves open() and open_bytes() return identical typed refusals. Exact results: fmt PASS; clippy --all-targets -D warnings PASS; wasm32 no-default-features check PASS; open_bytes+refusals 43 tests PASS; full locked no-fail-fast suite 92 tests and 0 doctests PASS; UBS_SKIP_RUST_BUILD=1 ubs .beads/issues.jsonl src/parquet_reader.rs tests/open_bytes.rs PASS, 0 criticals, 19 warnings and 19 info inventory findings; git pull --rebase up to date; git push PASS; GitHub CI 46104988980 PASS (quality and wasm); slot-2 cargo clean PASS, removed 2622 files / 750.0 MiB. Not verified: fuzzing or an exhaustive malformed-Parquet corpus beyond this reproducer and existing fixtures; downstream released shape/rvl binaries; non-macOS release artifacts. Bead remains open; never closed.
